# Appendix A: Installation and Setup {#sec-app-installation}

```{python}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
import sys
import data2thesis as dt
import pandas as pd
```

This appendix explains how to install everything the book uses, how to configure your working environment, and how to resolve the issues that most often arise. If you want to get started immediately, the short version is: install **Python**, install **Visual Studio Code**, create a virtual environment, and install the companion packages with `pip`. If you are not ready to install anything locally yet, every chapter's exercises can also be run directly in your web browser in the [interactive playground](../playground/index.html).

Software installers and websites update their appearance over time, so this appendix describes each step in clear terms. The essential configuration choices remain consistent across versions.

## What you need

| Software | What it is | Required? |
|---|---|---|
| **Python** (3.10+) | The programming language and computation engine | Yes |
| **VS Code** | Code editor with integrated terminal, plot viewer, and notebook support | Yes (or Positron) |
| **Positron** | Modern data science IDE by Posit, designed for Python and R | Optional |
| **Quarto** | Authoring tool that compiles research code into papers, books, and slides | Yes |
| **Scientific packages** | Libraries (`pandas`, `seaborn`, `scipy`, etc.) installed via `pip` | Yes |
| **data2thesis** | Companion package containing all Graduate Wellbeing Study datasets | Yes |

: The software used in this book {#tbl-software}

All of these tools are free and open source. Python should be installed first so that editors and tools can discover your Python interpreter automatically.

## Installing Python

Python is downloaded from the official Python Software Foundation website at [python.org/downloads](https://www.python.org/downloads/). Always download the latest stable release (version 3.10 or newer; 3.12 is recommended).

### Windows

1. On [python.org](https://www.python.org/downloads/windows/), download the **Windows installer (64-bit)**.
2. Run the installer. On the very first screen, **make sure to check the box: "Add python.exe to PATH"**. This is essential: it enables your terminal and code editor to find Python.
3. Click **Install Now**. If prompted with "Disable path length limit" at the end of the installation, click it to avoid Windows file-path truncation issues.

### macOS

1. On [python.org](https://www.python.org/downloads/macos/), download the macOS 64-bit universal installer (`.pkg`).
2. Run the package installer and accept the standard defaults.
3. After installation completes, navigate to your Applications folder, open the `Python 3.x` folder, and double-click `Install Certificates.command` to ensure secure network connections (SSL) function properly when downloading datasets and packages.
4. Alternatively, if you use Homebrew, you can install Python directly from Terminal:
   ```bash
   brew install python
   ```

### Linux

Python comes pre-installed on most modern Linux distributions. On Debian/Ubuntu distributions, ensure the development packages and package manager are installed:

```bash
sudo apt update
sudo apt install python3 python3-pip python3-venv
```

### Checking the installation

Open your system terminal (Command Prompt or PowerShell on Windows; Terminal on macOS and Linux) and type:

```bash
python --version
```

If it prints `Python 3.12.x` (or any version 3.10+), Python is installed and accessible.

## Installing VS Code

1. Download **Visual Studio Code** from [code.visualstudio.com](https://code.visualstudio.com/) for your operating system.
2. Install the application using default settings. On Windows, check the boxes to add "Open with Code" to the context menu.
3. Open VS Code. On the left sidebar, click the **Extensions** icon (four square blocks, or press `Ctrl+Shift+X` / `Cmd+Shift+X`).
4. Search for and install:
   - **Python** (by Microsoft)
   - **Jupyter** (by Microsoft)
   - **Quarto** (by Posit PBC)

### Positron: A Dedicated Data Science Alternative

**Positron** ([positron.posit.co](https://positron.posit.co)) is a specialized code editor built by Posit for scientific data analysis in Python and R. It provides dedicated panes for Variables, DataFrames, and Plots out of the box. Everything taught in this book works identically in VS Code and Positron.

## Managing projects with virtual environments

In empirical research, package versions evolve. To prevent package updates from inadvertently altering your thesis calculations months later, create a **virtual environment** for your research project. A virtual environment is an isolated directory containing its own Python interpreter and set of installed libraries.

In your research project folder:

```bash
# 1. Create a virtual environment named .venv
python -m venv .venv

# 2. Activate the virtual environment
# Windows (PowerShell):
.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1
# Windows (Command Prompt):
.venv\Scripts\activate.bat
# macOS / Linux:
source .venv/bin/activate
```

When activated, `(.venv)` appears at the start of your terminal command line. In VS Code, press `Ctrl+Shift+P` (or `Cmd+Shift+P`), type `Python: Select Interpreter`, and choose the interpreter inside your `.venv` directory.

: Python packages used across book chapters {#tbl-packages}

To install all required packages into your virtual environment in a single command, run:

```bash
pip install pandas numpy openpyxl pyreadstat matplotlib seaborn scipy statsmodels scikit-learn xgboost torch shiny requests
```

### The student wellbeing data: the `data2thesis` package

The case-study data for Elaf's research is bundled in the companion package **`data2thesis`**. You can install it directly via `pip`:

```bash
pip install data2thesis
```

Verify that the package and dataset load properly:

```{python}
import data2thesis as dt

students = dt.load_students()
print(f"Loaded {students.shape[0]} students and {students.shape[1]} variables.")
```

All datasets are also available as direct CSV, Excel, and SPSS downloads on the [book website](https://polla-fattah.github.io/data2thesis_python/).

## Common problems and solutions

**`'python' is not recognized as an internal or external command`**
: Python was installed without checking "Add python.exe to PATH". Re-run the Python Windows installer, select **Modify**, and check the PATH option, or add your Python installation folder (e.g., `C:\Users\Username\AppData\Local\Programs\Python\Python312\`) to your system Environment Variables.

**`ModuleNotFoundError: No module named '...'`**
: The library is not installed in the currently active Python environment, or VS Code is pointing to a different Python interpreter. Open the VS Code Command Palette (`Ctrl+Shift+P`), select `Python: Select Interpreter`, and choose your project's `.venv`. Then run `pip install <package-name>`.

**`Execution of scripts is disabled on this system (Windows PowerShell)`**
: PowerShell on Windows restricts script execution by default. Open PowerShell as Administrator and run:
  ```powershell
  Set-ExecutionPolicy -ExecutionPolicy RemoteSigned -Scope CurrentUser
  ```
  This allows activating local virtual environment scripts.

**`File not found` when loading datasets**
: In research scripts, always use relative paths starting from the project root (e.g., `data/students.csv`), or use the helper function `dt.load_students()`. Avoid absolute paths like `C:\Users\Elaf\Desktop\data.csv`, which fail when shared with supervisors or collaborators.

**Restarting a clean session**
: If variables from earlier interactive runs are causing unexpected errors, restart the Python interactive kernel. In VS Code, click the **Restart** button at the top of the Interactive Window or notebook.
